kaps_punt: daar is baie verskillende soorte lewende dinge; lewende plante en diere kan al die sewe lewensprosesse uitvoer: voeding, groei, reproduseer, asemhaling, uitskeiding, sintuie, beweging; sommige dinge lyk nie lewendig nie (soos droë bone, droë gis, 'n bevrugte voëleier), maar kan weer 'leef' in die regte omstandighede

items.bewering: Rondom jou leef baie duisende soorte plante en diere.
items.bron: SANBI National Plant Checklist (2025): about 20 200 indigenous plant species in South Africa alone, before any animals are counted (opus.sanbi.org; repository.up.ac.za 'Taking stock of South Africa's flora'). 'Baie duisende' understates rather than overstates.

items.bewering: Die gras onder jou voete leef, en die kewer op die blaar leef ook.
items.bron: Grass is a plant and a beetle an insect; both are organisms showing the life processes (Twinkl teaching wiki 'Seven life processes', twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes).

items.bewering: Selfs broodmuf en kieme is lewende dinge.
items.bron: Bread mould (Rhizopus) is a living fungus (Milne Open Textbooks botany, milnepublishing.geneseo.edu/botany/chapter/rhizopus). 'Germ' is defined as a microorganism, especially one causing disease; Merriam-Webster's kids' sense: 'a microscopic living thing especially one that causes disease' (merriam-webster.com/dictionary/germ). CAVEAT for a person: 'kieme' includes viruses (KidsHealth, kidshealth.org/en/parents/germs.html; Merriam-Webster sense 3), and whether viruses are alive is genuinely debated. As the ordinary dictionary meaning the sentence is defensible at Grade 4; the real problem is what the lesson then claims every germ does - see the weerspreek item on the block's last sentence.

items.bewering: Die muf groei op ou brood, leef daarvan en versprei oor die brood.
items.bron: Rhizopus appears as growth on stale bread, its mycelium digests and absorbs nutrients from the food it grows on, and stolons spread it across the surface (Milne Open Textbooks botany; LibreTexts Biology 2.43 Rhizopus; EBSCO Research Starters 'Black bread mold').

items.bewering: Lewende dinge het al sewe die lewensprosesse, nie net een of twee nie.
items.bron: The sentence comes straight after 'Selfs broodmuf en kieme is lewende dinge', so it says that every germ carries out all seven processes. Germs include viruses (KidsHealth 'Germs: Bacteria, Viruses, Fungi, and Protozoa'; Merriam-Webster 'germ' sense 3, 'such as a bacterium or virus'). Outside a host cell viruses do not feed, grow, excrete or respond, and they cannot reproduce on their own (KidsHealth: viruses 'need to use another cell's structures to reproduce'; TutorChase IB notes on cells as the smallest units of life). Many disease bacteria cannot move either: Staphylococci lack flagella and pili (University of Nottingham repository, nottingham-repository.worktribe.com/OutputFile/854450), and Streptococcus is non-motile. The lesson's own germ block is careful ('Baie kieme eet, hulle groei en hulle maak nuwe kieme'), and this sentence undoes that care by making the claim universal. Even apart from germs, 'all seven' does not hold for every individual: a mule cannot reproduce but is accepted as living (University of Pennsylvania biology handout 'Characteristics of life', serendipstudio.org/exchange/files/characteristics of life SH.pdf). As the general Grade 4 'MRS GREN' rule for plants and animals the idea is fine; the fault is that here it is attached to germs.
items.regstelling: Narrow who the claim is about so that it no longer says every germ carries out all seven processes. One true version: plants and animals carry out all seven life processes, not just one or two (this is also how the lesson's own CAPS line puts it: 'lewende plante en diere kan al die sewe lewensprosesse uitvoer'). Alternatively, move the sentence away from the one naming broodmuf and kieme. Whatever the wording, the yeast reasoning later on (two observed processes as evidence of life) has to stay consistent with it. The writer should also check that the 'Elke lewende ding ...' sentences in the nutrition, excretion and senses blocks are not read as covering every germ.

items.bewering: Elke lewende ding het kos nodig om te lewe.
items.bron: Nutrition is one of the seven life processes. Organisms either take in food or make it, as plants do by photosynthesis (weet.co.za 'Lewende en nielewende dinge'; Twinkl 'Seven life processes'). True for cellular life. On the germ question see the weerspreek item above.

items.bewering: 'n Koei vreet gras, en 'n leeu vreet vleis.
items.bron: Cattle are grazing herbivores and lions are carnivores (weet.co.za: animals get their food from plants or other animals). These are standard examples of the two feeding types.

items.bewering: 'n Groen plant maak sy eie kos in sy blare met sonlig.
items.bron: Photosynthesis happens mainly in leaf mesophyll chloroplasts and is powered by light (Macmillan 'Physiology' ch. 4.7, digfir-published.macmillanusa.com/phelanphys3e/phelanphys3e_ch4_7.html). Green stems also photosynthesise, and in cacti they are the main site. 'In sy blare' is therefore the usual case rather than the only one, which is an acceptable Grade 4 simplification.

items.bewering: Lewende dinge word groter en sterker en verander bietjie vir bietjie.
items.bron: Growth is a lasting increase in size or mass, through more cells or bigger cells (Twinkl 'Seven life processes'; IGCSE MRS GREN revision page, express.adobe.com/page/4Dw4N/).

items.bewering: 'n Klein saadjie kan oor baie jare 'n boom word.
items.bron: Trees take years to decades to grow from seed: fast growers reach 3-5 m in about five years, and oaks take 20-40+ years (homefortheharvest.com 'How long for a tree to grow'). The sources are weak on exact figures, but 'oor baie jare' is safe across all of them.

items.bewering: 'n Kuiken kry vere en word 'n hen of 'n haan.
items.bron: Domestic chicks hatch in down, and juvenile feathers replace it over the first weeks; Chu's study of brown Leghorn plumage puts visible juvenile feathering at about six weeks (University of Edinburgh ERA, era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/29675). A chick grows into a hen or a rooster.

items.bewering: Lewende dinge kan nuwe lewende dinge van hulle eie soort maak.
items.bron: Reproduction is one of the seven life processes (Twinkl; weet.co.za). 'Kan' read as a statement about kinds of living thing is true. Individual exceptions (mules) do not make a 'can' statement about kinds false.

items.bewering: 'n Hen lê eiers, en uit 'n bevrugte eier kom 'n klein kuiken.
items.bron: A chick comes from a fertile egg after 21 days of incubation (Virginia Tech Virtual Farm 'Poultry development', sites.ext.vt.edu/virtualfarm/poultry/poultry_development.html; Penn State 4-H 'Where chick life begins'). Saying 'bevrugte' correctly leaves out unfertilised table eggs.

items.bewering: Baie plante maak sade, en uit een saad kom 'n nuwe plant.
items.bron: Seeds germinate into new plants (University of Vermont 'Northeast Dry Bean Production Guide', uvm.edu). 'Baie plante' correctly leaves out ferns and mosses, which make spores. That a few species, such as citrus, can give more than one seedling from one seed does not make the Grade 4 statement false.

items.bewering: Die meeste lewende dinge gebruik suurstof om energie uit hulle kos te kry.
items.bron: Almost all animals, most plants and most fungi are obligate aerobes (Wikipedia 'Obligate aerobe'; BioNinja IB 'Modes of respiration', ib.bioninja.com.au). These groups make up the great majority of described species. Among bacteria and archaea the picture is mixed, and many are anaerobic. Read as 'most kinds of living thing', the claim is true. 'Die meeste' is the right quantifier: 'alle' would be false.

items.bewering: Jy haal asem met jou longe, en 'n vis gebruik sy kieue.
items.bron: Fish gills extract oxygen from water passing over them (Wikipedia 'Fish gill'; Macmillan 'Biology' ch. 39.6). Lungs are the human organs of gas exchange (Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Education, 'Excretion by the lungs, skin and kidneys', learn.moe.gov.tt).

items.bewering: 'n Plant neem ook lug in deur klein gaatjies in sy blare.
items.bron: Stomata are tiny pores, mostly on the underside of leaves, through which gases enter and leave (LibreTexts Biology (Kimball) 16.2D 'Gas exchange in plants'; Harrison et al. 2019, PMC7065165).

items.bewering: Elke lewende ding se liggaam maak afval wat moet uitkom.
items.bron: Excretion, the removal of the waste products of metabolism, is one of the seven life processes (Twinkl; weet.co.za 'skei afvalstowwe uit'). True for cellular life. On germs see the weerspreek item above.

items.bewering: Jy sweet, jy blaas lug uit en jy gaan toilet toe.
items.bron: Sweat carries urea and salts, exhaled air carries waste carbon dioxide and water, and urine is excreted by the kidneys (Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Education, 'Excretion by the lungs, skin and kidneys'). Note: faeces are strictly egestion, not excretion (GeeksforGeeks / Vedantu 'Difference between egestion and excretion'). 'Jy gaan toilet toe' covers urination, so the sentence is true, but the writer should not narrow it to faeces.

items.bewering: 'n Plant maak kos en laat die suurstof wat oorbly deur sy blare uit.
items.bron: Oxygen is a by-product of photosynthesis and leaves the plant through the stomata (LibreTexts Kimball 16.2D; TutorChase IGCSE 'Significance of stomata in photosynthesis'). 'Wat oorbly' is accurate: the plant uses some of it in its own respiration and releases the rest.

items.bewering: Elke lewende ding merk op wat om hom gebeur en reageer daarop.
items.bron: Sensitivity, responding to changes in the surroundings, is one of the seven life processes (Twinkl 'What is Mrs Gren?'). True for cellular life, including plants and bacteria. On germs see the weerspreek item above.

items.bewering: Jy ruik die kos, en jy word honger.
items.bron: Food odours raised appetite scores and food intake against a no-odour control. Smell triggers the cephalic-phase response, including salivation and insulin release (Wageningen University 'Does the nose know?', research.wur.nl; Proserpio et al., air.unimi.it).

items.bewering: 'n Plant het nie oë of ore nie en merk tog die lig op.
items.bron: Plants have no eyes but carry photoreceptors (phytochromes, phototropins, cryptochromes) throughout their tissues (Macmillan 'Plant biology' ch. 26.5, digfir-published.macmillanusa.com/pol2e/pol2e_ch26_5.html; John Innes Centre 'How do plants sense the world around them?').

items.bewering: Lewende dinge beweeg self, party vinnig en party baie stadig.
items.bron: Movement is one of the seven life processes, and in plants it is often slow or internal (Twinkl 'Seven life processes'). The lesson's own glossary entry (''n hele lewende ding of net 'n deel daarvan') allows the part-movement that plants show. The claim that every germ moves is dealt with in the weerspreek item.

items.bewering: 'n Bok hardloop vir gevaar weg.
items.bron: Antelope and goats are prey animals that flee from predators. This is a standard example of animal movement (Twinkl 'Seven life processes', movement section).

items.bewering: 'n Plant se stingel buig na die lig
items.bron: Phototropism: the shaded side of the stem grows faster and the shoot bends toward the light (Macmillan 'Biology' ch. 31.25, digfir-published.macmillanusa.com/morris2e/morris2e_ch31_25.html).

items.bewering: baie blomme maak saans toe.
items.bron: Nyctinasty: tulips, crocuses, daisies, dandelions, poppies and gazanias open each morning and close each night (Live Science 'Why do flowers close up at night?', livescience.com/34569; BBC Science Focus on poppies). 'Baie' rightly leaves out the night-blooming flowers that do the opposite.

items.bewering: Party dinge lyk glad nie lewendig nie en leef tog.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Dormant seeds, dried yeast and fertile eggs are alive but inactive (Distillique, a South African source: dried yeast cells are 'in a dormant state'; Penn State 4-H 'Where chick life begins'; UVM dry bean guide).

items.bewering: 'n Droë boontjie lê stil in 'n sakkie, maar in nat grond groei dit.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Viable dry bean seeds germinate in 3-4 days when kept moist and warm (University of Vermont 'Northeast Dry Bean Production Guide 2016', uvm.edu). Warmth matters too, but nat grond in ordinary conditions supplies it.

items.bewering: Droë gis word wakker in warm water met 'n bietjie suiker.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Active dry yeast is dehydrated yeast in a dormant state, revived by rehydrating in warm water at about 35-40 °C (Distillique, distillique.co.za, 'Active dried yeast: re-hydration or direct addition?'; Drayman's 'Dry yeast rehydration'). Sugar starts visible activity (Tinkerlab 'Yeast sugar experiment'; USDA ARS AgLab 'Experimenting with yeast'). Mapping of 'word wakker': dormant becomes active again. It holds, and it does not suggest the yeast was dead. The word 'warm' is correct, and it should not be strengthened to 'warm' meaning hot, because hot water kills yeast.

items.bewering: Die gis kry kos uit die suiker en maak 'n gas as afval. Die gas vorm borrels in die water.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Yeast breaks down sugar by fermentation, giving carbon dioxide and alcohol. The water bubbles as the yeast produces carbon dioxide (BBC Science Focus 'Why does yeast make bread rise?'; Tinkerlab; USDA ARS AgLab yeast experiment PDF, ars.usda.gov).

items.bewering: Kos kry en afval uitkry is twee van die sewe lewensprosesse. Die borrels wys dat die gis doen wat lewende dinge doen.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: Nutrition and excretion are both in the seven (weet.co.za; Twinkl). The carbon dioxide is a metabolic waste product of the yeast (BBC Science Focus). The inference from bubbles to life is the standard school demonstration (USDA ARS AgLab, which also uses a no-sugar comparison).

items.bewering: In 'n bevrugte eier wag die begin van 'n klein kuiken. As die eier warm gehou word, groei die kuiken waar jy dit nie kan sien nie.
items.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
items.bron: After laying, cooling arrests the early embryo below 'physiological zero', and it can resume development when warmed by the hen or an incubator (Virginia Tech Virtual Farm 'Poultry development'; Penn State 4-H 'Where chick life begins'; PMC9033001 on chicken embryo diapause). Development inside the shell is hidden. The 'wag' personification maps correctly onto this pause.

items.bewering: Kieme is lewende dinge wat te klein is om te sien.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: Germs are microscopic microorganisms (KidsHealth 'Germs: Bacteria, Viruses, Fungi, and Protozoa'; Merriam-Webster kids' sense 'a microscopic living thing'). The same viral caveat applies as in the first block. As the ordinary meaning of the word this is acceptable at Grade 4, and it is flagged here so a person can see it.

items.bewering: Honderde kieme kan langs mekaar op die punt agter hierdie sin lê.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: Microbe Online 'Size of bacteria' (microbeonline.com): about 500 bacteria 1 µm long could be placed end to end across the period at the end of a sentence. A university answer key gives about 1 000. Viruses are smaller still. Mapping: 'langs mekaar' (in a line across the dot) is what the sources measure, so 'honderde' matches. Filling the dot's area would give far more, so the claim understates if anything.

items.bewering: Baie kieme eet, hulle groei en hulle maak nuwe kieme, net soos ander lewende dinge.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: Bacteria take nutrients from their environment, grow and divide (KidsHealth 'Germs'). 'Baie' rightly leaves out viruses, which cannot reproduce or grow on their own (KidsHealth: they need another cell's structures to reproduce).

items.bewering: Met 'n mikroskoop kan 'n mens hulle wel sien.
items.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
items.bron: Bacteria can be seen with a light microscope, and viruses need an electron microscope (I'm a Scientist, MRC Festival 2018, 'Can you see bacteria cells and viruses under a microscope?', archive.imascientist.org.uk). An electron microscope is still a microscope, so the general statement holds.

items.bewering: lewensprosesse: Die sewe dinge wat saam wys dat iets lewe.
items.bron: The seven life processes (MRS GREN) together characterise living things (Twinkl 'What is Mrs Gren?'; weet.co.za). Read alone, the entry says the seven together show life. It does not say every organism shows each one, so it does not carry the fault in the first block.

items.bewering: voeding: Om kos te kry of kos te maak vir jou liggaam.
items.bron: Nutrition is taking in food (heterotrophs) or making it (autotrophs, plants) (weet.co.za; Twinkl).

items.bewering: groei: Om groter en sterker te word en van binne te verander.
items.bron: Growth is a lasting increase in size or mass, often with development (Twinkl; IGCSE MRS GREN page). 'Sterker' and 'van binne verander' are loose but not false for a growing organism.

items.bewering: reproduseer: Om nuwe lewende dinge van jou eie soort te maak. Dit word ook voortplanting genoem.
items.bron: weet.co.za uses 'voortplant' for this life process, and reproduction is producing offspring of the same kind (Twinkl). 'Voortplanting' is the noun for the act the entry describes.

items.bewering: asemhaling: Om energie uit jou kos te kry. Die meeste lewende dinge gebruik suurstof uit die lug of die water daarvoor.
items.bron: Respiration as a life process is releasing energy from food in cells, not just breathing (TutorChase IGCSE 'Seven essential life processes'). Most animals, plants and fungi are obligate aerobes (Wikipedia 'Obligate aerobe'; BioNinja), and fish take oxygen from water (Wikipedia 'Fish gill'). Read alone, the entry is the correct scientific sense. 'Die meeste' is correctly not 'alle'.

items.bewering: uitskeiding: Om die afval wat jou liggaam maak weer uit te kry.
items.bron: Excretion is the removal of metabolic wastes produced by the body's cells (GeeksforGeeks 'Difference between egestion and excretion'). 'Afval wat jou liggaam maak' correctly leaves out undigested food.

items.bewering: sintuie: Die dele waarmee 'n lewende ding raaksien wat om hom gebeur.
items.bron: Sense organs or receptors detect stimuli. In plants the photoreceptors are in tissues such as the shoot tip, not in organs (Macmillan 'Plant biology' ch. 26.5). 'Dele' is broad enough to cover plant parts, and it fits the study text's 'n Plant het nie oë of ore nie'.

items.bewering: beweging: Wanneer 'n hele lewende ding of net 'n deel daarvan beweeg.
items.bron: Twinkl 'Seven life processes': movement includes plants moving parts, slowly or internally. The definition is circular but not false.

items.bewering: kieue: Die dele langs 'n vis se kop waarmee hy in water asemhaal.
items.bron: Gills lie on either side of the head behind the mouth cavity, under the operculum in bony fish, and take oxygen from water (Wikipedia 'Fish gill'; Macmillan 'Biology' ch. 39.6).

items.bewering: gis: 'n Klein lewende ding wat deeg laat rys.
items.bron: Baker's yeast is a single-celled fungus whose carbon dioxide makes dough rise (University at Buffalo news 2020 'Meet baker's yeast'; BBC Science Focus 'Why does yeast make bread rise?').

items.bewering: broodmuf: Muf wat op ou brood groei en van die brood leef.
items.bron: Rhizopus is a saprophytic fungus on stale bread that takes its food from the bread (Milne Open Textbooks botany; LibreTexts 2.43).

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'germ': a microorganism causing disease; kids' sense 'a microscopic living thing especially one that causes disease'. 'Kan' correctly allows harmless germs (KidsHealth). Same viral caveat as in the study text.

items.bewering: mikroskoop: 'n Toestel wat baie klein goed baie groter laat lyk.
items.bron: A microscope magnifies objects too small to see. Bacteria can be seen with a light microscope and viruses with an electron microscope (I'm a Scientist, MRC Festival 2018).

items.bewering: bevrugte eier: 'n Eier waarin die begin van 'n kleintjie kan groei.
items.bron: A fertile egg holds an early embryo that develops into a chick under incubation (Penn State 4-H 'Where chick life begins'; Virginia Tech Virtual Farm). 'Kan' is right: development needs warmth.

items.bewering: waterdamp: Water in die vorm van 'n gas wat niemand kan sien nie.
items.bron: Water vapour is an odourless, transparent gas, and the visible 'steam' cloud is condensed liquid droplets (London South Bank University Water Structure and Science, water.lsbu.ac.uk/water/steam.html; Scientific American 'How does bathwater give off steam?'). (No study block uses the word waterdamp. That is noted for the record only and is not a finding about truth.)

items.bewering: Jou pa sit droë gis in warm water met 'n bietjie suiker. Ná 'n rukkie is die water vol borrels.
items.bron: Yeast with sugar in warm water bubbles within minutes (Tinkerlab 'Yeast sugar experiment'; USDA ARS AgLab).

items.bewering: 'n Plant op die vensterbank buig na die venster toe. (Implies two visible life processes: sensing light and moving.)
items.bron: Phototropism means sensing light and bending toward it (Macmillan 'Biology' ch. 31.25). The bending happens through growth, so growth could also be argued for. 'Watter twee' still has a defensible answer, so this is not a falsehood.

items.bewering: Noem drie dinge wat lyk of hulle nie leef nie, maar wat wel leef.
items.bron: The lesson supplies three valid answers: dry bean, dry yeast and fertilised egg (sources as above).

opsomming: One fault: the first block says 'kieme' are living and then that living things have all seven life processes, which teaches that every germ feeds, grows, excretes, senses and moves. Viruses are germs and do none of this on their own, and many disease bacteria cannot move. The writer must narrow that sentence (e.g. to plants and animals) or move it away from the germs. Everything else checks out, including the bacteria-on-a-full-stop comparison and both uses of 'die meeste'. Separately, a person should know that 'kieme is lewende dinge' is defensible only as the dictionary sense, because whether viruses are alive is debated.
